properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 24 at 9:52AM MDT until September 24 at 12:45PM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Eddy County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 1245 PM MDT.

* At 952 AM MDT, the public reported water flowing over roadways
leading to road closures. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain have
fallen near Carlsbad and upstream in Dark Canyon Draw. Water from
Dark Canyon Draw will continue flowing towards Carlsbad. Although
rainfall has ended, flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Carlsbad, Carlsbad North, Avalon, Whites City, Cavern City Air
Terminal, Living Desert State Park, Otis and Lake Avalon.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 24 at 5:11AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**TROPICAL STORM NOLO CONTINUES TO STRENGTHEN AND MOVE SLOWLY
NORTHWARD TOWARDS THE BIG ISLAND**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Big Island East, Big Island
Interior, Big Island North, Big Island South, Big Island
Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala, and Kona

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 460 miles south-southeast of Honolulu or about 340 miles
south-southwest of Hilo
- 14.9N 156.2W
- Storm Intensity 60 mph
- Movement Stationary

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Nolo will continue to strengthen as it drifts slowly
northward towards the Big Island through Friday. Nolo is then expected
to make a turn to the west Friday night, passing south of the Big
Island Saturday.

Little change with the expected onset of conditions with this package,
with damaging tropical storm force winds reaching the Big Island as
early as midday Friday, and dangerous hurricane force winds possible
by Friday night. Tropical storm watches may be needed for other
islands should Nolo move closer to the state.

Bands of intense showers and thunderstorms associated with Nolo will
reach the Big Island as early as later today. Excessive rainfall is
possible which could lead to locally catastrophic flash flooding and
mudslides, mainly on windward and southeast Big Island. Flooding can
occur even in areas not usually prone to flooding. Outer rain bands
associated with Nolo are expected to reach the smaller islands, and
will be enhanced by the terrain, particularly on Maui. Storm total
rainfall amounts greater than 20 inches are possible on the Big
Island, with localized amounts of 35 inches. On Maui, rainfall amounts
greater than 10 inches are possible, with localized amounts of
20 inches.

Swell generated by Nolo could bring very large and rough surf and
dangerous rip currents for south and southeast facing shores,
especially for the Big Island.

Tornadoes and large waterspouts will be possible associated with Nolo,
mainly over and near the Big Island, along and to the right of the
track of the tropical cyclone.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
devastating impacts across the Big Island. Potential impacts include:
- Extreme rainfall flooding may prompt numerous evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may overwhelmingly overflow their banks
in many places with deep moving water. Small streams, creeks,
canals, arroyos, and ditches may become raging rivers. In
mountain areas, deadly runoff may rage down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter numerous structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Numerous places where flood waters may cover escape
routes. Streets and parking lots become rivers of raging water
with underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become very
dangerous. Numerous road and bridge closures with some weakened
or washed out.

Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
limited to extensive impacts across Maui County.

* WIND:
Prepare for life-threatening wind having possible devastating impacts
across the Big Island. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Structural damage to sturdy buildings, some with complete roof
and wall failures. Complete destruction of mobile homes. Damage
greatly accentuated by large airborne projectiles. Locations
may be uninhabitable for weeks or months.
- Numerous large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Many roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Many bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Widespread power and communications outages.

Also, prepare for life-threatening wind having possible limited to
extensive impacts across Maui County.

* SURGE:
Prepare for locally hazardous surge having possible limited impacts
across the Big Island. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across
the Big Island. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

If in a place that is vulnerable to high wind, such as near large
trees, a manufactured home, upper floors of a high-rise building, or
on a boat, plan to move to safe shelter.

If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the ocean or a large inland lake, in a low-lying or poor
drainage area, in a valley, or near an already swollen river, plan to
move to safe shelter on higher ground.

Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of
others.

When securing your property, outside preparations should be concluded
as soon as possible before conditions deteriorate. The onset of
strong gusty winds or flooding can cause certain preparedness
activities to become unsafe.

Be sure to let friends and family members know of your intentions for
weathering the storm and your whereabouts. Have someone located away
from the threatened area serve as your point of contact. Share vital
contact information with others. Keep cell phones handy and charged.

Check on those who may not be fully aware of the situation or who are
unable to make personal preparations.

If you are a visitor, know the name of the county or parish in which
you are located and where it is relative to current watches and
warnings. If staying at a hotel, ask the management staff about their
onsite disaster plan. Listen for evacuation orders, especially
pertaining to area visitors.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

There is a threat from tornadoes with this storm. Have multiple ways
to receive Tornado Warnings. Be ready to shelter quickly.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Honolulu HI around 11 AM HST, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 24 at 10:55AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau. The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at around 28.2 feet through the next 5 days. Additional
fluctuations are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 24 at 4:48AM HST until September 26 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
Intensifying Tropical Storm Nolo is expected to bring heavy flooding
rain to the eastern end of the state over the next few days. The
exact track of the dangerous tropical cyclone remains somewhat
uncertain, but significant heavy rain is likely over windward and
southeast Big Island.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Big Island, Maui, Lanai, Molokai, and Kahoolawe.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture on the north side of Nolo will bring heavy showers
later today and tonight over Big Island and spread to Maui.
Windward and southeast Big Island and windward Maui are the most
likely to experience heavy rain due to the slow moving tropical
cyclone, with considerable flooding possible over portions of Big
Island Friday and Saturday. Other islands in Maui County are at
risk as well.
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Anchorage; Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River; Lower Matanuska Valley
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 24 at 6:01AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
Strong southeast winds will start to increase as early as tonight
as a front lifts north across the Gulf of Alaska. Timing of peak
winds will be late Friday morning through Friday night, then
gradually tapering Saturday. Winds through Turnagain Arm will bend
away from west Anchorage early Friday, but could bend into
Anchorage later Friday night into Saturday morning. Periods of
rain will accompany the strong winds for Turnagain Arm and the
Anchorage and Eagle River Hillsides, but Anchorage Bowl and the
MatSu should remain mostly dry until Saturday afternoon.

Anchorage Hillside and Turnagain Arm (including South Anchorage):
Winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts 40 to 55 mph.

Anchorage Bowl, Knik River Valley through Butte and Palmer:
Winds 10 to 25 mph with gusts 25 to 35 mph. Brief, isolated gusts
to 40 mph is possible the Butte and Palmer area Friday afternoon.

Please use caution if driving or towing a high profile vehicle,
or if planning any outdoor activities with easily lofted objects.

NWSheadline: STRONG WINDS ALONG TURNAGAIN ARM, THE ANCHORAGE HILLSIDE, AND KNIK RIVER VALLEY TONIGHT THROUGH SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 24 at 5:33AM AKDT until September 26 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels on average of 1.5 to 2.5 feet above the
normal highest tide line near Kwigillingok. Southeast winds 35
to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected Thursday. South
winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts to 50 mph expected Friday.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast including Kwigillingok and
Kipnuk.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be multiple peaks in water
levels for the Kuskokwim Delta Thursday morning through
Saturday morning coinciding with high tide cycles and strong
southerly winds. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts to 60
mph Thursday afternoon will diminish early Friday until the
low pressure system moves west of the coast by Friday
afternoon. Then, winds will become southerly at 30 to 40 mph
with gusts to 50 mph by Friday afternoon. Winds gradually
weaken but remain southerly through Saturday.

For Kwigillingok, water levels reach 1.5 to 2.5 feet above the
normal highest tide line on Thursday, coinciding with the passage
of a frontal system. Water levels could reach up to 5 feet in a
worst case scenario. If water levels rise to 2.5 feet, impacts
would be comparable to the August 2024 storm.

For Kipnuk, the highest water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line are expected on Friday as a low pressure
system moves west of the coast and winds become southerly. Water
levels could reach 2 to 3 feet in a worst case scenario.

For more information regarding potential local flood impacts,
please reference maps.dggs.alaska.gov/akfit/
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 24 at 9:13AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is currently at Flood Stage 2.3 feet and
is forecast to continue to rise through Minor Flood Stage into Sunday
due to an ongoing period of northerly winds and tidal effects.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...From this morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 2.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is at flood stage and will continue to rise
to a crest of 2.8 feet Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.9
feet on 10/17/1999.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1130 AM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Colleton; Charleston
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 24 at 8:39AM EDT until September 24 at 10:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one foot of inundation
above ground level expected along shorelines and tidal
waterways (7.4 to 7.6 feet Mean Lower Low Water at Charleston).

* WHERE...Coastal Colleton and Charleston Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 PM this
afternoon to 10 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...This will result in some roads becoming impassable
and minor flooding of properties. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 7:10 PM today
at Charleston. Saltwater inundation will be possible several hours
before and after high tide.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Horry; Coastal Georgetown
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 24 at 8:11AM EDT until September 24 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, Strong north to south
long shore current is in place. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
up to one foot of inundation above ground level expected in
low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Horry and Coastal Georgetown Counties.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 9 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Vulnerable causeways to and from local beaches will
experience minor coastal flooding. Low-lying roads and
locations along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal
creeks will observe minor coastal flooding. Check with local
officials for the latest information regarding coastal flood
impacts and closures. Longshore currents can sweep swimmers
and surfers into rip currents, piers, jetties, and other
hazardous areas. It may sweep swimmers off their feet, making
it difficult to return to shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Caution should be used when in or near the water. Check with
lifeguards before entering the ocean for possible hazards you may
be swept into.

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

dangerous surf conditions.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Mountains; Quay County; Curry County; Roosevelt County; De Baca County; Chaves County Plains; Eastern Lincoln County; Southwest Chaves County
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 24 at 5:35AM MDT until September 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east-central and southeast New Mexico,
including the following areas, in central New Mexico, Eastern
Lincoln County and South Central Mountains. In east central New
Mexico, Quay, Curry, Roosevelt, and De Baca Counties. In southeast
New Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rounds of showers and storms will continue through tonight.
Rainfall rates up to 2 inches per hour will have the potential to
produce rapid runoff, especially during the afternoon and evening
hours on Thursday. Soils are becoming increasingly saturated from
persistent rainfall over the past couple of days, further
elevating the risk of flash flooding. Rainfall amounts will
generally range from 1 to 2 inches, with isolated totals up to 3
inches.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, near rivers and streams, and in locations
where the ground is already saturated from recent heavy rainfall.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued. Never drive through flood
waters. Most flash flood deaths occur in automobiles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE TONIGHT

properties.areaDesc: Monroe Upper Keys
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued September 24 at 7:32AM EDT until September 25 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Upper Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
properties.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 24 at 7:12AM EDT until September 24 at 1:15PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Roane County in central West Virginia...
Western Braxton County in north central West Virginia...
Calhoun County in north central West Virginia...
Gilmer County in north central West Virginia...
South Central Ritchie County in northwestern West Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 115 PM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Glenville, Sutton, Grantsville, Gassaway, Cedar Creek State Park,
Arnoldsburg, Normantown, Stumptown, Shock, Rosedale, Nicut,
Millstone, Cedarville, Tanner, Mount Zion, Orma, Wilsie, Big
Springs, Burnt House and Frametown.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Currituck
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 24 at 6:19AM EDT until September 25 at 7:00AM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8
to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
a high risk of rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
two to three feet of inundation above ground level expected in
low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Eastern Currituck County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 4 PM EDT Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EDT Friday. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Widespread flooding of vulnerable areas will result
in an elevated threat of property damage to homes and
businesses near the waterfront and shoreline. Water will be 2
to 3 feet above ground level in some areas resulting in a
sufficient depth to close numerous roads and threaten homes
and businesses. Flooding will extend inland from the
waterfront along tidal rivers and bays resulting in some road
closures and flooding of vehicles.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.description:

Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Saturday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 AM EDT Saturday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant beach erosion is expected.
Breaching of sand dunes is possible. Moderate tidal flooding
could continue into the weekend. Cannot rule out major tidal
flooding impacts, especially within the back bays.
properties.instruction:

flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.

officials.

https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and

to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or

expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued September 23 at 11:07PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
HLSHFO

This product covers the Hawaiian islands

**NOLO CONTINUES TO SLOWLY MOVE NORTHWARD TOWARDS THE BIG ISLAND**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Big Island East, Big Island
Interior, Big Island North, Big Island South, Big Island
Southeast, Big Island Summits, Kohala, and Kona

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 460 miles south-southeast of Honolulu or about 340 miles
south of Hilo
- 14.9N 156.0W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement North or 360 degrees at 2 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Nolo will continue to slowly strengthen as it drifts
generally northward towards the Big Island. Nolo is expected to make a
turn to the west Friday night, passing south of the Big Island
Saturday.

Little change with the expected onset of conditions with this package,
with damaging tropical storm force winds reaching the Big Island as
early as Friday morning, and dangerous hurricane force winds possible
by Friday night. Hurricane or tropical storm watches may be needed for
other islands should Nolo move closer to the islands.

Bands of intense showers and thunderstorms associated with Nolo will
reach the Big Island as early as Thursday. Excessive rainfall is
possible which could lead to locally catastrophic flash flooding
and landslides, mainly on windward and southeast Big Island. Flooding
can occur even in areas not usually prone to flooding. Outer rain
bands associated with Nolo are expected to reach the smaller islands,
and will be enhanced by the terrain, particularly on Maui. Storm
total rainfall amounts greater than 20 inches are possible on the
Big Island, with localized amounts of 35 inches. On Maui, rainfall
amounts greater than 10 inches are possible, with localized amounts
of 20 inches.

Swell generated by Nolo could bring very large and rough surf and
dangerous rip currents for south and southeast facing shores,
especially for the Big Island.

Tornadoes and large waterspouts will be possible associated with Nolo,
mainly over and near the Big Island, along and to the right of the
track of the hurricane.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
devastating impacts across the Big Island. Potential impacts include:
- Extreme rainfall flooding may prompt numerous evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may overwhelmingly overflow their banks
in many places with deep moving water. Small streams, creeks,
canals, arroyos, and ditches may become raging rivers. In
mountain areas, deadly runoff may rage down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter numerous structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Numerous places where flood waters may cover escape
routes. Streets and parking lots become rivers of raging water
with underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become very
dangerous. Numerous road and bridge closures with some weakened
or washed out.

Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
limited to extensive impacts across Maui County.

* WIND:
Prepare for life-threatening wind having possible extensive impacts
across the Big Island. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Considerable roof damage to sturdy buildings, with some having
window, door, and garage door failures leading to structural
damage. Mobile homes severely damaged, with some destroyed.
Damage accentuated by airborne projectiles. Locations may be
uninhabitable for weeks.
- Many large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. Several bridges, causeways, and
access routes impassable.
- Large areas with power and communications outages.

Also, prepare for dangerous wind having possible limited to
significant impacts across Maui County.

* SURGE:
Prepare for locally hazardous surge having possible limited impacts
across the Big Island. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across the Hawaiian islands, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across
the Big Island. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

If in a place that is vulnerable to high wind, such as near large
trees, a manufactured home, upper floors of a high-rise building, or
on a boat, plan to move to safe shelter.

If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the ocean or a large inland lake, in a low-lying or poor
drainage area, in a valley, or near an already swollen river, plan to
move to safe shelter on higher ground.

Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of
others.

When securing your property, outside preparations should be concluded
as soon as possible before conditions deteriorate. The onset of
strong gusty winds or flooding can cause certain preparedness
activities to become unsafe.

Be sure to let friends and family members know of your intentions for
weathering the storm and your whereabouts. Have someone located away
from the threatened area serve as your point of contact. Share vital
contact information with others. Keep cell phones handy and charged.

Check on those who may not be fully aware of the situation or who are
unable to make personal preparations.

If you are a visitor, know the name of the county or parish in which
you are located and where it is relative to current watches and
warnings. If staying at a hotel, ask the management staff about their
onsite disaster plan. Listen for evacuation orders, especially
pertaining to area visitors.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

There is a threat from tornadoes with this storm. Have multiple ways
to receive Tornado Warnings. Be ready to shelter quickly.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Honolulu HI around 5 AM HST, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Up to 1 foot of inundation is
possible for sound-side flooding when winds become more
northerly late Thursday and Friday. For the Beach Hazards
Statements, dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves
expected, and strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 11 PM EDT Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Portions of Highway 12
will be inundated. Low lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be
inundated. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw
a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck
and back injuries. Strong longshore currents will create
dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 12:12 PM Thursday.
properties.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Entrance U. S. Waters Strait Of Juan De Fuca.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds can cause hazardous seas which could

and/or location is still uncertain. It is intended to provide
additional lead time for mariners who may wish to consider
altering their plans.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Southeast Suffolk County.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Life-threatening rip currents are likely for all
people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches
should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal Flood Advisories will likely be
needed for Friday PM and Saturday AM high tides. Localized
moderate coastal flooding can also not be ruled out.
properties.instruction:

you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 24 at 2:44AM EDT until September 25 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 8 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 8 AM this morning to 4
AM EDT Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 8 AM EDT
this morning through late Friday night. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, from 5 PM this afternoon to 11 AM EDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong, southward flowing longshore
current is expected to develop in the surf zone, in addition to
the other hazards.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Modoc County Except for the Surprise Valley
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 23 at 11:00PM PDT until September 24 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In CAZ285...Fire weather zone 285.

* WIND...Southwest 12 to 20 mph with gusts of 30 to 35 mph.

* HUMIDITY...Daytime humidities of 11 to 15 percent.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

properties.areaDesc: Gallia, OH; Vinton, OH
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 23 at 7:26PM EDT until September 24 at 3:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding due to runoff from excessive rainfall over the last
few days is occurring.

* WHERE...Central Gallia County in southeastern Ohio...
Southeastern Vinton County in southeastern Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along Raccoon Creek and its tributaries is
occurring. Numerous roads remain closed due to flooding. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 720 PM EDT, county officials reported that flooding of the
Raccoon Creek is occurring across the warned area. State Route
124 in southern Vinton County remains closed due to flooding. In
the City of Vinton, State Route 325 at State Route 160 is closed
due to flooding. State Route 554 between Rio Grande and Bidwell
is closed due to flooding.
- The Raccoon Creek gauge at Adamsville has breached action stage
and continues to slowly rise.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Rio Grande, Vinton, Wilkesville, Adamsville, and Radcliffe.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 23 at 2:57PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A strong low southeast of Hooper Bay will provide southeasterly
winds from Thursday to Saturday. This will likely result in minor
erosion on the Bay side of Hooper Bay as well as minor water
rises to around 1 to 2 feet above the normal high tide line with
each high tide cycle from Thursday afternoon to Saturday morning.
Strongest wind gusts, up to 55 mph are expected to occur between
7 AM and 10 PM Thursday. There may be a gust to 60 mph but it
would be infrequent. After 10 PM Thursday, winds will mainly
weaken and be less than 50 mph Friday and Saturday.

NWSheadline: Minor Water Level Rises and Gusty Winds in Hooper Bay

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 23 at 1:18PM AKDT until September 26 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Interior Kuskokwim Delta, including Kwethluk, Kasigluk,
Bethel, Napaskiak, Napakiak, Oscarville, and other nearby villages.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rain in combination of persistent high water
levels and storm surge may result in flooding of rivers, creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Area creeks and streams are running high and could flood
with more heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A strong storm projected to move into the eastern Bering Sea will
bring heavy rainfall and storm surge to the area. The Kuskokwim
River is currently running high, with statistics showing the
river is already above the 90th percentile in flow for this time
of year. 1 to 2 inches of rainfall across the Kilbuck Mountains,
as well as across the lower Kuskokwim, is likely to exacerbate
high water levels for the Kwethluk River, Johnson River / tundra
villages, as well as other smaller tributaries and sloughs of the
Kuskokwim.

Confidence is moderate-to-high that flooding of low-lying areas
will occur for Kwethluk and Kasigluk, where high-water was
reported last week. Confidence is lower for flooding elsewhere
and will be dependent on the rainfall amount and degree of
compounding effects from coastal surge and tide cycle.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SATURDAY AFTERNOON

properly tuned.
